decisions.reason: As a very recently launched crate in the firm's core plastics handling business, it would usually be kept because management can still justify weak early traction as a ramp-up issue despite its lower public commitment on the website.
The foldable large container has a dedicated page, signaling visible commitment and sunk development effort, so escalation of commitment makes withdrawal within a year unlikely.
A stackable plastic crate fits the firm's established product logic, and with only a short time on the market management would tend to continue rather than admit failure quickly.
The medium-duty rackable pallet is close to the firm's core industrial offering, so prior investment and the ability to blame any slow sales on market adoption support keeping it.
Because the spill-retention pallet was given its own page and likely reflects a deliberate strategic push in logistics and safety plastics, management would be reluctant to reverse course so soon.

The plastic pallet with load retainers has visible website prominence and strong overlap with the firm's main product family, which under escalation of commitment favors continued support rather than exit.
